subject.title: [Bug]:  Session status blind spot | Sessions in done state excluded from context saturation monitoring — agents run dead for hours undetected

question: What native behavior should OpenClaw apply when a terminal `done` session is at or above its context budget: diagnostics-only alerting, automatic cleanup/recovery, or no native action until the live failure mode is proven?
rationale: Source proves the monitoring gap, but choosing the alert surface, threshold semantics, and recovery behavior is product policy rather than a mechanical code repair.

options.title: Define diagnostics-first alerting
options.body: Add a native diagnostics/health warning for saturated terminal sessions first, then consider cleanup or recovery only after live evidence proves it is safe.

options.title: Require live repro before design
options.body: Keep the issue blocked on logs or a focused scenario that proves restart-to-done plus silent delivery before choosing the product behavior.

options.title: Build automatic recovery
options.body: Treat saturated terminal sessions as recoverable stale state and add cleanup or lane-release behavior, with higher compatibility and false-positive risk.

recommendation.title: Define diagnostics-first alerting
recommendation.body: Add a native diagnostics/health warning for saturated terminal sessions first, then consider cleanup or recovery only after live evidence proves it is safe.

likelyOwner.reason: The central decision lands closest to the diagnostic heartbeat and session attention owner boundary.
